candidates.title: The AC Remote Treaty
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 1: Evening living room. Aachu is wrapped in a shawl and socks, Zuv is visibly warm, and the AC remote sits between them on the coffee table.
Slide 2: Aachu quietly reaches for the remote like she is moving evidence; Zuv notices from the other side of the sofa.
Slide 3: Zuv redirects a small fan toward himself while Aachu secures the blanket corner, both pretending this is a mature negotiation.
Slide 4: The remote rests centered between them like a peace treaty; fan angled at Zuv, Aachu tucked warm, both smug and comfortable.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: A clean living-room frame with the AC remote as the only disputed object: Aachu bundled, Zuv warm, both eyelines pulled toward the remote.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The remote is placed neutrally between them, the room has been divided into two climates, and both look quietly victorious.
candidates.visual_potential: Very readable. One room, one hero prop, strong body language, clean upper wall space for baked handwritten text. The joke is visible before any caption saves it.
failure_risks: Do not show tiny AC temperature numbers; the remote should read as a remote, not require legible digits.
Avoid generic couch cuddling; the treaty geometry must stay visible.
Do not exaggerate sweating or shivering into cartoon acting.

candidates.title: The Food Photo Waiting Room
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 1: A restaurant or dining-table scene. Zuv holds a fork midair while Aachu rotates the plate for the perfect food photo.
Slide 2: Aachu adjusts the angle; Zuv lowers the fork with heroic restraint, eyes locked on the food.
Slide 3: Zuv is recruited as lighting assistant, holding a napkin or spoon just outside the plate like a reflector.
Slide 4: Photo done. Aachu immediately gives him the first bite while he is still holding the napkin like crew.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Zuv frozen with fork hovering inches from the food while Aachu calmly turns the plate under warm light.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Aachu feeds him the first bite after making him wait, turning the irritation into a tiny reward.
candidates.visual_potential: Strong send-trigger and very stageable if the plate, fork, phone, and napkin stay large and simple. Good tabletop composition with upper negative wall space.
failure_risks: Phone screen content must stay blank or abstract; no tiny photo-interface text.
Arm and hand anatomy can get messy if the overhead-phone pose is too ambitious.
Restaurant menus, labels, or table clutter must not become unreadable microtext.

candidates.title: The Laundry Line Diplomacy
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 1: Balcony or indoor drying corner. Zuv has proudly hung one huge towel across the whole line while Aachu stands with wet clothes and a clothespin in hand.
Slide 2: Aachu folds the towel smaller; Zuv holds the pegs like he has been promoted to assistant.
Slide 3: They build a neat rhythm together: her dupatta, his shirt, shared towel, small socks, all with breathing room.
Slide 4: A tiny disagreement over one last clothespin becomes a silent handoff, not a fight.
Slide 5: They step back under the line and admire the laundry like a gallery, with the paired socks centered as the visual punchline.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: One oversized towel hogging the whole clothesline, Aachu holding the remaining wet clothes, Zuv looking proud of a job technically done badly.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Both stand under a perfectly balanced clothesline, admiring it with ridiculous satisfaction as the smallest pair of socks steals the frame.
candidates.visual_potential: Best frame. Fresh, tactile, airy, domestic without being generic. Balcony wall or sky gives perfect upper-middle text space, and the clothesline creates a natural slide-to-slide visual spine.
failure_risks: Too many garments will clutter the frame; keep each slide to one line and a few readable pieces.
Avoid clothespins in mouths or tangled fingers; hands should stay simple and visible.
Do not use printed clothing text or laundry labels.

candidates.title: The Parcel Opening Committee
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 1: One unopened delivery on the floor or coffee table. Aachu reaches for the tape; Zuv pretends not to care but already has the scissors.
Slide 2: Zuv holds the box flaps open while Aachu lifts the tissue paper, both leaning in from separate sides.
Slide 3: Bubble wrap spills out and becomes more interesting than the actual item.
Slide 4: The ordered item sits to the side while both of them pop bubble wrap together, fully invested in the wrong part of the parcel.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: A blank delivery box between them, scissors in Zuv's hand, Aachu's hand on the tape, both faces readable and separated by the box.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The real purchase is abandoned while they sit with the bubble wrap, enjoying the shared nonsense like it was the point all along.
candidates.visual_potential: Clean prop comedy. The box creates safe spacing between faces, the bubble wrap gives tactile charm, and the floor/table staging can stay intimate without crowding.
failure_risks: No readable address labels, brand stickers, or package text.
Scissors and box-flap hands need simple poses to avoid anatomy noise.
Do not let the frame become an unboxing ad; the couple behavior must stay the subject.

top_pick.title: The Laundry Line Diplomacy
top_pick.why: It is the freshest visual frame: one location, tactile props, natural separated faces, strong slide progression, and a payoff that does not need microtext or a quote-card rescue.

visual_risks: Do not show legible numbers, package labels, menu text, phone UI, or clothing print; all become microtext risk.
Keep faces three-quarter, profile-separated, or divided by props; avoid crowded face merges.
Limit each slide to one hero object plus two supporting props.
Preserve upper-middle negative space for later warm-charcoal handwritten text.
Every slide needs a visible action, not just softness.

slide_count_hints.The AC Remote Treaty: 4 slides. Longer than that repeats the same thermostat beat.
slide_count_hints.The Food Photo Waiting Room: 4 slides. Can compress to 3, but the assistant transformation is funnier with one extra beat.
slide_count_hints.The Laundry Line Diplomacy: 5 slides. The line needs room for setup, repair, co-building, tiny dispute, and gallery-style payoff.
slide_count_hints.The Parcel Opening Committee: 4 slides. More than 4 will turn the parcel props into clutter.
